Embedded evaluators might sound unusual in tech but it's pretty normal in other industries. Big banks have federal examiners with desks in the building and every nuclear plant in the US has inspectors who work on site full time. One non-model thing I'm very excited we announced today with Fable 5.1 is Enterprise Frontier Safeguards (EFS).

Even if you're not a CEO/CISO, this blog post is a look into how big companies are thinking about AI adoption which is important to understand if you're interested in how AI might diffuse across industry.

Companies are giving agents more and more access to internal systems. With traditional zero data retention, there's been no way to spot patterns in what agents might be doing across sessions on these systems.

EFS is ZDR++. It's ZDR built for a world with agents. A company's data stays in its own cloud, and an automated monitoring layer we built flags risky patterns to its team.

I think of this as an observability and risk mitigation layer for agents. My guess is it will become a standard requirement from enterprises for running increasingly powerful AI on their systems.

For those just starting to test Fable, here's four tips for using it more effectively:
1. Give it bigger, more ambitious tasks than what previous models could handle.
2. Use xhigh/high effort as your default for best performance, med for faster interactive sessions.
3. Rework your skills and CLAUDE.mds. Instructions written for prior models anchor Fable to stale patterns, let it use its own judgment first.
4. Move from providing tasks to providing objectives. Describe what done looks like and how to verify it, then let Fable find the path (/loop and /goal are built for this)
